$comment: S3178: the source-controlled boundary between the two Wear artifacts.
The `standard` flavor is what Google Play distributes and is an ALLOWLIST: a capability is absent from it
unless it is named under `standardAllowlist`. `noLegal` is the sideload artifact and keeps everything.
Every noLegal-only category below names the permissions, components and routes that carry it, so returning
one capability to the store variant is a reviewable edit of this file rather than a silent manifest change.
Read by scripts/quality/assert-wear-store-boundary.ps1, which judges the two merged manifests against it.

standardAllowlist.$comment: The whole surface the first Play publication offers. Nothing outside this list may appear in the standard merged manifest or its route graph. S3362: `settings/permissions` is on the list because the route IS registered in every edition (S3226), even though the store artifact declares no runtime permission and therefore draws no menu entry to reach it - the list names the graph, not what a tap can find. S3555: the notification permission left the sideload-only voice category for this list - Wear OS 4+ silently drops an ongoing-activity notification without it, and the stopwatch must show its WO-V4 indicator; the rest of the voice category stays sideload-only.

libraryContributed.$comment: Declarations no source file in this module writes - they arrive from a dependency manifest or from the debug build type. They are allowlisted by name rather than by a wildcard, so a library that starts contributing something sensitive still surfaces as an unnamed declaration. S3362: androidx.core's DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION is named twice because it is built from the applicationId, so the debug merge carries the `.debug.` infix and the RELEASE merge does not - allowlisting only the debug spelling failed the gate against the artifact that actually ships.

noLegalOnly.$comment: Media read/write and viewing: the watch's own media, the browse graph, the players and the document viewer.
The recorder, its foreground microphone session and the note list it writes.
Network sources, SMB aliases, credential entry and the stream catalog. Credential entry was already withheld by S2486; here the transport itself goes too.
The Network Monitor mini-program, the watch's own system report and the Tourist telemetry dashboard - device and usage data Play treats as sensitive.

The GPS fix the Tourist dashboard is built on - speed, altitude, coordinates, satellites, trip distance and sun times. Its own category rather than a line under diagnostics because Play reviews location against the store description on its own (S2013), and the route it serves is already noLegal-only, so permission and capability leave the store artifact together (S3115).
Visible Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth adapter state, read by the Network Monitor. Separate from the diagnostics category because the permission family is reviewed on its own.
Heart rate, blood pressure and activity/motion readings. Already confined by S2457, S2458 and S2995; recorded here so the one policy answers for the whole boundary.
The phone may ask this watch for a picture of its own screen over the Data Layer. No permission carries it - the component is the whole capability.

Handing a file to another application on the watch, and moving content between the watch and the paired phone. S3362: the clipboard program joins it - its only action is a Data Layer round trip, so without a companion the store artifact could offer nothing but an empty clipboard and a disabled button.

S3362: the water flashlight and the distress signal. Both consume every pointer event on the initial pass so a wet wrist cannot dismiss them, which is the gesture WO-V3 asks for on almost every screen and neither of the two exemptions it names. They also draw full-bleed white against WO-V13, and the signal raises the alarm stream to its maximum and strobes at about three flashes a second. No permission carries either one - the screens ARE the capability - which is why they read as store-safe until the review criteria are applied to the gesture rather than to the manifest.

The entry points that reach the categories above without passing through a screen. FOREGROUND_SERVICE is here rather than under one capability because every foreground service this module starts belongs to an excluded category.
